title: Climbing Kilimanjaro Over 50
excerpt: Many people climb Kilimanjaro in their fifties, sixties and beyond. Here is what to think about when you are not in your twenties anymore.
body:
Age itself is not a barrier on Kilimanjaro. Plenty of climbers reach Uhuru Peak in their fifties, sixties and even later. What matters is health, preparation and enough time.

## Start with your doctor

Have a check-up before you commit, especially if you have heart, lung or blood pressure conditions or take regular medication. Discuss altitude, medication and vaccinations.

## Choose more days

Older climbers often do very well because they walk at a steady pace and do not rush. Give yourself extra time: eight days on [Lemosho](/blog/kilimanjaro-lemosho-route-guide/) or nine on the [Northern Circuit](/blog/kilimanjaro-northern-circuit-guide/).

## Look after your joints

- Trekking poles reduce strain on knees, especially on the way down.
- Train on descents as well as climbs.
- Good boots with cushioning help.

## Recovery

Recovery overnight becomes more important with age. A comfortable sleeping mat, a warm sleeping bag and good food make a real difference. Our partner can arrange extra comfort such as a thicker mattress.

## Huts or tents?

If you prefer a solid roof, [Marangu](/blog/kilimanjaro-marangu-route-guide/) is the only route with huts. Choose the six-day version.

## Travel insurance

Check that your insurance covers trekking to 6,000 m and helicopter evacuation, and whether there is an age limit. See [travel insurance for Kilimanjaro](/blog/kilimanjaro-travel-insurance/).

## Combine it

Many travellers over 50 add a relaxed [safari](/blog/kilimanjaro-and-safari-combined/) afterwards. [Plan your trip with us](/travel-proposal/).
